intent: Widen the five-sensor array to ±0.054 m at 0.027 m steps, as the Integrator's rule requires after iteration 3 left s-bend and slalom line losses at 1.0 with max_error at 0.062 to 0.067 m. Keep mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m, which were the best turn-authority settings tested. Change only the sensor span so the effect of reach can be read cleanly. Expected: s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0 with max_error below about 0.055 m, and oval progress holds near 0.12 or improves.
learning: Iterations 2 and 3 showed mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m did not clear the s-bend and slalom losses, so turn authority has reached its limit in the geometry. Read the next race as follows: if s-bend and slalom line losses reach 0 with max_error below 0.055 m, sensing reach was the constraint and the span should be kept. If losses stay at 1 with max_error at the limit, the geometry is at its range and the next gains must come from the controller. If progress on oval falls below 0.12, return to wheel_track 0.10 m.
rationale: Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m, mass 0.6 kg, ±0.045 m sensors) scored 55.14, up slightly from iteration 2 (54.15) but still below the baseline's 62.32. The s-bend and slalom still lost the line once per run (line_loss_events 1.0), with max_error 0.0618 and 0.0673 m, so narrowing the track did not clear them. Oval progress stayed at 0.121, so the 0.09 m track did not cost progress, and oval line losses (0.6) were no worse than before. The Integrator's stated rule for this case applies: with mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m, line losses still at 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.054 at 0.027 m steps and keep sensor_size 0.012 m. Mass is kept at 0.6 kg because iteration 2 showed it reduces oval losses (1.05 to 0.35 with the same sensors). The 0.09 m track is kept because it did not hurt progress. The remaining turn-authority levers (mass, track) have now been tried, so reach is the lever left. Expected result: the tape stays in view to about 0.06 m off centre, so the robot gets an earlier, larger correction on the s-bend and slalom. I expect s-bend and slalom line losses to fall toward 0 and max_error to drop below about 0.055 m. The 12 mm footprint is unchanged and the body and wheel radius are unchanged, so the change reads cleanly. The body width still cannot widen the off-track limit (0.06 m).
